title: Vibe-coded 90% of my multiplayer game to finally ship a project that sat unfinished for 3 years
author: Smugg_Dev
selftext:
Started this as a proof-of-concept for my Associate's Degree in Software Development. Never finished it. It sat shelved while I went and got a full-time dev job. A while back I decided to pick it back up alone, and actually ship it.

The only way that was realistic around a full-time job was leaning hard into AI-assisted development, probably 90% of the actual code was vibe-coded rather than hand-written line by line. I directed every system (custom decks, mode design, matchmaking/deck logic, a live voting flow for a 100-viewer streamer mode, backend/frontend architecture), but the implementation itself was mostly me describing what I wanted and iterating on what came back, not typing every function myself.

The result is **Smugg.io**: a multiplayer browser deduction game, guess your opponent's secret character before they guess yours. Built on Vite + React on the frontend.

Honestly the hardest part wasn't the AI-generated code, it was catching the subtle bugs AI introduces that don't throw errors, just quietly break game logic. Curious how others here are handling review/debugging discipline when most of the code isn't something you wrote yourself line by line.
